samples.summary: `runFilesDownload` feeds a *successful* response into `upstreamErrorJson`, which now synthesizes `HTTP 200`
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/files/download.ts:56 keeps the pre-existing condition `if (!res.ok || !res.bytes)`. Under the old code the branch printed `res.data ?? { error: { code: 'HTTP_ERROR' } }`, i.e. a bare code with no message. `upstreamErrorJson` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:245) unconditionally builds its message from `res.status`, so an `ok: true` response that somehow lacks `bytes` now reports `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 200"}}` — an upstream failure message for a 2xx. `HttpClient.downloadFileDocument` (http-client.ts:286-293) always sets `bytes` on the ok path, so the path looks unreachable today, but the caller's condition and the new helper's contract no longer agree. Fix belongs at download.ts:56 (split the `!res.bytes` case into its own, non-upstream error).

samples.summary: `login` still reports backend failures as plain text + `process.exit(1)`, contradicting the invariant the new comment states
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:203 asserts "Every command that talks to the backend routes its `!res.ok` branch through here". `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:62`, `:79` and `:96` each check `!res.ok` on a direct `fetch` and emit unstructured text (`Failed to fetch workspaces (HTTP 403)...`) followed by `process.exit(1)`, so no `{error:{code,message}}` envelope ever reaches stderr for the login namespace. Pre-existing, not introduced here, but it makes the newly documented invariant false for an agent that branches on `error.code` and it was not considered when the rest of the namespaces were converted.

samples.summary: `UpstreamHttpError` is exported but referenced nowhere outside its own module
samples.evidence: Grep for `UpstreamHttpError` across the repo returns only packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:187/194/214 (the class and comments); the new test file imports `forwardUpstreamError`, `outputError` and `upstreamErrorJson` but not the class (packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:9-13). knip's unused-exports check is one of the enforced lanes, so either give it a consumer (e.g. asserting `instanceof` in a test) or drop the `export`.
